title: Concept: Content-Security-Policy font-src allows a wildcard source
description: The Content-Security-Policy font-src directive contains a bare wildcard, so webfonts may come from any origin. A face chosen by an attacker can make rendered text observable through the glyph requests the browser makes, which is a slow but script-free leak channel.
applicability: HTTPS responses that send Content-Security-Policy with an explicit font-src directive.
risk: Rendered text can be inferred through attacker-chosen fonts; LOW severity because the leak is slow and needs both an injection point and a readable page.
